sections.overview: The Kakadu dunnart is a small dasyurid marsupial described from Australia’s Northern Territory.
sections.identification: The species was formally described in 1994; the database sources consulted do not summarize field marks.
sections.habitat: Its original description identifies it as a species of the Northern Territory’s stony woodlands.
sections.diet: The species accounts consulted do not establish a distinct prey list.
sections.behavior: Species-specific behavior is not detailed in the accounts used here.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide species-specific reproductive observations.
sections.ecology: It shares the genus Sminthopsis with the Julia Creek dunnart S. douglasi; see that profile.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database reports a global IUCN category of Near Threatened.
